title: Valid CA Public Key File Record Layout
applicability: Separate EMV CA key-file/key-load data that supports EMV transactions using Segment 100 and Segment 130.

businessRequirements.title: A CA Public Key file shall use the CA_KEYS file name, version, comma-separated records, and CRLF termination.
Each CA Public Key record shall contain valid expiry date, SHA-1 hash indicator, RSA algorithm indicator, RID, index, modulus, exponent, and checksum fields.
An EMV Segment 100/130 transaction shall use CA key configuration consistent with the applicable EMV AID and public-key data.

testCases.positive: Valid CA_KEYS file and CA public-key record
EMV AID resolves to valid configured CA key

testData.reason: File name, version, delimiter, and CRLF termination are structural checks on a synthetic CA_KEYS file.
Record layout and checksum algorithm can be validated against a self-consistent synthetic key record; does not require a genuine production RSA key.
Confirming that a real EMV AID resolves to the correct production CA key requires the actual First Data/network-issued key file; a synthetic key cannot validate genuine AID-to-key resolution.

testDataReadinessSummary.note: File header and record layout are structurally synthesizable; genuine AID-to-key resolution requires a real production key file.

testDataStatus: No CA_KEYS file or external EMV key-load artifact is currently available. File header and record layout can be validated with synthetic data; the AID-to-key link cannot.
remaining: Author a synthetic CA_KEYS file/record for structural validation.
Obtain the real CA key-file/key-load artifact for the AID-to-key link check; do not synthesize it.
